newsitem.title: NORWAY: DDB may seek takeover target in Norway - report.
newsitem.headline: DDB may seek takeover target in Norway - report.

text.p: Knud Soerensen, head of Denmark's Den Danske Bank (DDB), was quoted on Tuesday as saying the bank may expand in neighbouring Norway through a friendly takeover of a Norwegian bank.
Soerensen, in an interview with the Norwegian daily Aftenposten, did not identify a possible takeover target, but said DDB may want to penetrate the Norwegian market more deeply.
DDB, which opened an office in Oslo in 1995, will be seeking customers among large and medium-size Norwegian companies and may later also focus on small firms and private customers, he said.

"A further effort like that would require a network of branches, which we don't have today," Soerensen was quoted as saying. "If we decide to expand our activity it would most naturally happen through a takeover of a Norwegian bank.
"But we have no takeover plans, and we don't know if there are any candidates for the moment," he said.
Analysts have speculated that the Danish market leader may bid for Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth largest bank.
Fokus, which is owned primarily by foreign investors, is currently trying to fight off a hostile takeover bid from Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 regional savings banks out to carve it up.
Soerensen said DDB, which took a controlling interest in Sweden's Ostgota Enskilda Bank in March, would never attempt a hostile takeover.
"We don't push but should an opportunity arise we are more than willing to consider a takeover," he told Aftenposten.
He said he believed the Nordic financial sector would be dominated by three or four big players across the borders in a few years.
Such a consolidation would chiefly take place through takeovers, he suggested.
